title: IED security documentation survey: catalogue inventory
note: Rules that turn each vendor's own catalogue listing into inventory entries. A rule reads one field: 'url', 'slug' (last path segment) or 'text' (model name and, where the vendor gives one, its one-line product type; during enrich, the product page's title and opening words). The first matching rule wins and an exclusion always beats a category. Lifecycle values are the states fixed under 'definitions'; a rule may add 'vendor_label' to keep the vendor's own word (legacy, obsolete, active mature) without letting it decide the state. A lifecycle_text rule reads the product page and may carry 'within', the number of opening characters it looks at, so that a notice about one variant further down the page does not mark the whole product. Change a rule and re-apply it with: survey.py inventory --from <previous inventory>.

definitions.legacy: A device is counted as legacy only when the vendor states, in a dated source, that support for it has ended (end of support, end of service, end of life). A discontinued device without such a statement is reported in its own group and is not legacy. The protocol a device speaks, a security feature it lacks and the age of its manual never decide this.

lifecycle_statuses.currently_supported: Listed in the vendor's current catalogue on the inventory date without a notice of discontinuation, or stated by the vendor to be on sale and supported.
lifecycle_statuses.discontinued_supported: The vendor states that manufacture or sale has ended and that support continues.
lifecycle_statuses.discontinued_support_not_stated: The vendor states that manufacture or sale has ended; no statement about support was found.
lifecycle_statuses.end_of_support: The vendor states that support has ended. This is the legacy group.
lifecycle_statuses.unknown: None of the above is established. This includes products the vendor only labels legacy, products under a last-time-buy notice and families that are partly withdrawn.

definitions.release_date: Recorded separately when a vendor source states it. It never decides lifecycle status.
